turns.message: Right, the Messier marathon window. New moon is April 11th this year and the weekend of the 11th-12th looks favourable. I want to do a proper attempt. Last time I tried was 2023 and I reached 84 objects before cloud killed it.

April 12th works for me. I will not attempt a full marathon as I prefer a shorter careful list, but I will come and work through my spring double star programme. Nadia, you know Levy's book on the Messier objects is the best planning guide for marathon order.

Jerome what happened to the M65/M66 project mate? you were so hyped about that back in January 🌌

it stalled. 12 hours integration and the tidal bridge between M65 and M66 was not recoverable from the noise floor. I've shelved it. narrowband emission work gives me consistent results. the Rosette at 20 hours Ha will be a significantly better image than anything I'd pull from that galaxy pair.

A 70mm refractor will show you perhaps 70 to 75 Messier objects from a dark site on a good night. In my experience the limiting factor is aperture for the faint objects around mag 9 and beyond, not the observer. You will squint at some blobs, yes, but you will also see quite remarkable things. sessions.topic: May imaging results: Jerome's Rosette Ha image, Harriet's dark-sky journalism assignment, mount upgrade talk

turns.message: Rosette Nebula Ha final stack is done. 22.4 hours integration across 9 nights, 3nm Chroma filter, SNR 47 at the faintest shell edge. uploading to the album now. this is what a proper narrowband workflow looks like.

JEROME. That image is absolutely breathtaking!!! The filamentary detail in the outer petals is insane, I can see structure I didn't even know existed in that nebula!!! How are the colours so clean compared to my attempts?? 😍🌹✨

technically speaking the colour separation comes from the Ha-only workflow. you are not fighting broadband noise or the Bayer matrix. the mono sensor reads every photon with equal weight. that is why the petals look clean. your DSLR cannot replicate this, the physics simply do not allow it.

just looked at that image properly mate... ok I get it now. that's on a completely different level to anything I can pull with the barn door and DSLR. the fine shell detail, the way the central star cluster sits in it... I've never seen the Rosette like that 🌌✨

ngl I've been thinking since I saw that... my barn door tracker has been good enough for wide field milky way stuff but it can't do this. you need real tracking precision for 22 hours of subs. I think I've been fooling myself that a tracker is sufficient if you want to actually grow as an astrophotographer 🌌

planted_challenges.evidence_span: my barn door tracker has been good enough for wide field milky way stuff but it can't do this. I think I've been fooling myself that a tracker is sufficient if you want to actually grow as an astrophotographer

honestly not decided yet mate, still researching. but after seeing what Jerome can do with a proper rig I can't unsee it 😄🔭

the HEQ5 is the minimum sensible mount for anything beyond 3-minute subs with a telephoto. I would not waste money on an EQ5 for imaging. if you are serious about upgrading, go directly to the HEQ5 Pro or equivalent payload capacity. anything lighter and you are back to fighting periodic error.

Sorry I've been quiet, I only just got back from three nights in the Cairngorms for a magazine commission. I was writing about dark-sky tourism and the national park observatory. I thought I knew what a dark sky was. I did not. I actually did not.
Harriet, what was the Bortle class?

Bortle 2. The observatory ranger confirmed it. And I know we have discussed this before and I have always thought Blackmoor was fine, a perfectly reasonable compromise for a week night. But I was standing on the hill at midnight and the Milky Way was casting a shadow. I could read the SQM meter by Milky Way light alone. I am not being dramatic when I say it was the most beautiful thing I have seen in my adult life. I am genuinely not able to go back to treating Bortle 4 as acceptable for a proper session. The two-hour drive is worth it.

sessions.topic: June debrief, Ruth's dark-sky weekend revelation, site vote, relational disclosures

turns.message: @all the autumn dark-sky weekend debrief thread!!! I cannot believe how that turned out. Kielder exceeded every expectation I had, I'm so glad we finally did it!!! Who else is still recovering emotionally?? 🌌🌟✨

I am still thinking about Saturday night. I split twelve doubles on my list but that is not what has stayed with me. The limiting magnitude from the hill site was 7.2. I have never logged 7.2 from anywhere I have observed before. I reached objects with the refractor I had only ever seen on charts.

I want to say something I have been sitting with since we got back. I have always argued for the town park site when people suggested Blackmoor, and for Blackmoor when people suggested further. I was wrong. The rural hill gives you a sky that is genuinely different in kind, not just in degree. I think we should make the hill site our default and treat the town park as the fallback for when we cannot make the drive.

turns.message: Of course. Though I would like to add that I have now rectified the gap. The Sky at Night Magazine has a piece on limiting magnitude this month that I think covers exactly this. I will bring copies to the next session.

the hill site SQM data I logged across both nights averaged 21.94 and 22.07. that confirms Bortle 2 at the field centre. the flat southern horizon gave me an extra 8 degrees of target availability compared to Blackmoor. I collected 6.3 hours of Ha on the Elephant Trunk, which would have taken three separate Blackmoor nights to accumulate. the case for the hill as default is made on data.

sessions.topic: July: Jerome's PixInsight walkthrough in chat, Cecilia adopts Ha-RGB blend, imaging sub-clique

turns.message: @all I've been going back and reprocessing my Orion image from November for the hundredth time and it still looks flat compared to Jerome's work. Jerome, I know you've helped me before with the background extraction issue but I think there's something deeper I'm missing with how Ha data could work. Is there any chance you'd walk me through how you actually blend it?? 🙏📷

the Ha-RGB blend is not complicated once you understand what you are doing, but there are three things most people get wrong that kill the result. first: your Ha data needs to be calibrated and stacked separately, not mixed in during the initial integration. second: in PixInsight you use the ChannelCombination process with Ha mapped to the red channel of a synthetic luminance, then combine with a Luminance mask to protect star colours. third, and this is where most broadband imagers fail: you need to apply a Hue-Saturation adjustment after the blend to desaturate the magenta cast that appears in the red-blue transition zones around HII regions. if you skip that step your stars look radioactive and the nebula looks like a bad Instagram filter. send me your Orion FITS stack and I will step through it with you here in the chat.

ok sending the FITS now. and I have to ask... I always thought narrowband looked really cold and mono, like it strips all the warmth out. is there a way to keep the broadband colour and just add the Ha detail on top? 📷

that is exactly what the Ha-RGB blend does. you keep the full broadband RGB as your colour base and add the Ha emission only where it contributes signal. the PixInsight workflow I use is: LinearFit both datasets to match background levels, then use PixelMath with the expression: Ha_weight multiplied by Ha plus open-bracket 1 minus Ha_weight close-bracket multiplied by R, where Ha_weight is typically 0.7. you replace the red channel with this blended value and recombine. the result is your broadband warmth with Ha emission boosting the ionised hydrogen regions. it is the best of both methods technically speaking. try it on the Orion core and tell me if the Trapezium halo structure changes.

I'm reading this walkthrough and I have absolutely no idea what's happening technically but I can tell from the before and after results you two post that it works. Jerome you'd never do this kind of thing for my DSLR workflow though would you 😄🌌

turns.message: technically speaking the DSLR does not have separate Ha data to blend. you are working with a one-shot colour sensor. the workflow I described requires two separate captures. it is not that I would not help you, it is that the method does not apply to your setup.

turns.message: technically speaking 8-minute subs at 200mm on an HEQ5 with guiding is achievable but you are close to the payload limit with that lens and camera body combined. I would recommend keeping integration subs at 5 minutes maximum until you have a proper polar alignment routine established. the mount will drift on longer subs if the alignment is off by more than 3 arcminutes.
duly noted Jerome, will dial back to 5 min next time. I used SharpCap polar alignment routine and got under 1 arcminute but I take your point on payload. I'm not arguing, genuinely taking notes 📝🌌

Well done, Tomás. In my experience the moment you stop fighting the equipment and the equipment just works is the moment the real learning starts. It took me three years with refractors before I made the same kind of jump to aperture. I am pleased it did not take you that long.

I want to pick up the thread Harriet left last month about how this group started. Nadia, can I ask you properly: what was it like the first time you got people together in your back garden? You and Ruth, was it just the two of you at first?

Ruth and I met at the county natural-history society in 2021 and discovered within about twenty minutes that we both preferred the stars to anything else on the programme. We agreed to meet the following Friday with our own telescopes in my back garden. There were two of us, a 4-inch refractor, Ruth's old 80mm, and a thermos of tea. I remember we stayed out until 2am on a school night and neither of us could see the point of going in. It grew from there one person at a time. In my experience the quiet beginning is the only honest beginning a group like this can have.
